results.title: Key Institutional Considerations for Designing EffectiveIndependent Verification Organizations
results.description: In recent months, a rash of agentic AI breaches – illegally hacking into government data (Kim 2026; Conger, Swanson, and Kang 2026), swarming into external repositories (Conger 2026), and leaking user information (Seetharaman, Satter, and Horwitz 2026) – has ignited calls for a more mature assurance ecosystem comprising better measurement, evaluation, and reporting on AI tools in use. Independent verification organizations (IVOs) offer a potential answer. As currently envisioned, an IVO is a licensed, independent, expert-led body that impartially assesses whether an AI system meets specific safety, risk, and trustworthiness criteria (Fathom 2025; Smith, McKenzie, and Jones 2026).11 1 It is worth noting that these criteria have yet to be fully established or harmonized across state and federal levels.
